findings.title: First-use lock methods can commit incomplete coordination rows
findings.description: lock_daily_head(create_first=True) directly inserts an ACTIVE revision-zero S38 with no bundle, and lock_execution(create_first=True) directly inserts an APP_STARTED READY revision-zero S44. Both execute before idempotent_outcome constructs its RestrictedSqlSession. execute_command commits after operation returns and RepositoryTransaction.finish checks only registry, subject and exact leased-artifact identities. It never checks first_execution_head/first_execution_session or successful complete command bookkeeping. A legitimate internally authenticated owner operation can acquire the required guards, call the first-use method, and return normally; the raw insert commits without S39-S42/S27 success/S29 COMMITTED or S45 START, and without S02/S03/S04. The first-use completion assertions in RestrictedSqlSession.validate_completion cannot run on this path. This widens the repository owner capability beyond the packet's exact mandatory complete effects, even though the normal adapter path calls idempotent_outcome.
findings.authority: KL-019 Existing owner reuse and bounded missing capabilities: owner mutation/completion checks must prove exact newly inserted row identity and required complete effects; first-use row effects must roll back with the transaction. Frozen DB §5 T6/T7 and Protocol §2.1/§5.3/§5.5 require atomic command effects.
findings.verification: Independent source reachability inspection and a pure NoSql finish probe for CommitBundle/StartSession each with a first-use marker and satisfied finish-level registry/subject state both returned normally without checking command completion. This probe is a pure demonstration of the missing finish check, not PostgreSQL acceptance evidence.
findings.requested_change: Make outer transaction completion fail closed whenever either first-use row was inserted unless the exact new row and full successful T6/T7 effects completed through the owner in the same transaction. Add real PostgreSQL negative cases where an operation creates the first-use row and returns without idempotent completion; assert complete rollback, plus successful retry and existing owner regressions.

findings.title: Preflight receipt miss can route a historical retry through live registry denial
findings.description: publish, commit and start first call the receipt-only _replay, but after a miss their owner operation calls _registry before execution_historical_outcome. A retry can read no receipt, pause while the original identical command commits and a dependent artifact is revoked, then acquire the new registry gate. acquire_registry_lease rejects the committed revocation before the under-S01 historical receipt recheck runs. The successful identical historical outcome now exists, yet the retry returns a live guard rejection. There is no receipt-only fallback on that rejection. This does not grant execution, but fails the required historical ACK-loss/idempotent behavior after authority loss. The same-key contention test keeps live artifacts eligible, and the ACK-loss test starts its retry after the successful receipt already exists, so neither covers this schedule.
findings.authority: KL-019 execution_ack_loss_replay_dc oracle requires exact historical replay after authority loss/expiry/revocation; existing repository_transactions contract requires receipt-only replay without reacquiring registry/live work guards. Frozen DB §3 distinguishes historical successful outcome from current eligibility.
findings.verification: Independent inspection of receipt lookup and registry-then-history ordering yields the stated legal schedule. No DB lifecycle or live concurrency experiment was run by this reviewer.
findings.requested_change: Preserve receipt-only historical replay even when an initial lookup misses and the original result commits before a live guard rejects. Do not reverse S51/S01 lock order or convert a historical result into new permission. Add bounded real PostgreSQL barriers for preflight miss, original commit and real T2-GLOBAL revoke, then assert exact historical identities, replayed=true, executable=false and no duplicate effects.
